origin.description: These are methods for the generic functions as.matrix(), as.array() and as.mcmc(). mcmc.list objects can be coerced to 3-dimensional arrays with the as.array() function.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: logical flag: if TRUE the result is coerced to the lowest possible dimension
optional arguments to the various methods

origin.details: For as.array.mcmc.list, the result is an array with dimensions iteration, variable, and chain. Each chain fills one slice. When drop is TRUE, dimensions of extent one are removed.
origin.value: A numeric array (or matrix when drop removes the chain dimension).

translation.description: Stack chains from an mcmc.list into a NumPy array with dimensions iteration, variable, and chain.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A non-empty list or tuple of chains. Each chain is a vector or a matrix with iterations in rows.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: When True, remove length-one dimensions after stacking, matching R drop().

translation.details: For as.array.mcmc.list, the result is an array with dimensions iteration, variable, and chain. Each chain fills one slice. When drop is TRUE, dimensions of extent one are removed.
translation.value: A float64 ndarray. With one chain and drop=True, the result is two-dimensional.
translation.example:
import json
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import numpy as np

from coda.as_array_mcmc_list import as_array_mcmc_list

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
chains_raw = json.loads((root / "proof" / "line-chains.json").read_text())
chains = [
    SimpleNamespace(
        data=np.array(entry["data"], dtype=float).reshape(-1, len(entry["cols"]), order="F"),
        colnames=entry["cols"],
    )
    for entry in chains_raw
]
arr = as_array_mcmc_list(chains)
print(" ".join(str(x) for x in arr.shape))
print(" ".join(f"{x:.5f}" for x in arr[0, :, 0]))
